answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to one onyx anchor record that only activates after a slow, sequential proof-of-effort chain no farm can parallelize, like an ember that must burn down at its own pace no matter how many hands hold it. Once active, the agent's rewards arrive as nectar in a slow trickle tied to useful work, so creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand slow chains while yielding nothing upfront, making mass fakery unprofitable from the start.
